skill.name: video-edit
skill.description: Routes video editing requests to RunComfy models for restyling, background changes, packaging swaps, outfit edits, and reference-based motion transfer.
skill.summary: Route each video edit to a suitable RunComfy model and apply model-specific prompting.

security_audit.summary: All static alerts are Markdown syntax, placeholder URLs, documentation, or standard token storage guidance. The skill intentionally sends prompts and media locations to RunComfy, creating a third-party data disclosure risk.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before sending prompts or media URLs to RunComfy. Warn users not to submit sensitive media or reusable signed URLs.

content.user_title: Edit Videos with the Right RunComfy Model
content.value_statement: Choosing the wrong video model wastes time and weakens identity or motion consistency. This skill routes each edit to a suitable RunComfy model and prompt pattern.
actual_capabilities: Routes general restyling, background changes, and packaging swaps to Wan 2.7 Edit-Video.
Routes reference-based character motion transfer to Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control.
Routes localized outfit, lighting, and background edits to Lucy Edit Restyle.
Builds RunComfy inputs with preservation, audio, resolution, duration, and orientation options.
Explains route-specific media limits and retry-relevant CLI exit codes.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, an authenticated account or token, and accessible source media URLs.
Selects one model per request and cannot blend multiple editing routes.
Wan, Kling, and Lucy impose different duration, resolution, format, and aspect-ratio limits.
RunComfy services process requests remotely and fetch supplied media.

use_cases.title: Polish Social Videos
use_cases.description: Restyle short talking-head clips while preserving faces, motion, lip movement, and original audio.

use_cases.title: Refresh Product Creative
use_cases.description: Replace a product background or packaging design while retaining framing, hand movement, and camera motion.

use_cases.title: Transfer Character Motion
use_cases.description: Apply motion from a reference clip to a target character with identity and spatial constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Make One Localized Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit [video URL]. Preserve the subject's face and motion. Change only [outfit, lighting, or background]. Keep the original audio.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused visual change

prompt_templates.title: Replace a Background
prompt_templates.prompt: Replace the background in [video URL] with [new setting]. Preserve the subject, framing, camera movement, lip movement, and original audio.
prompt_templates.scenario: Controlled talking-head or product background edit

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Reference Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the packaging in [video URL] using [reference image URL]. Preserve hand movement, framing, camera motion, and all other product details.

prompt_templates.title: Map Reference Motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Transfer motion from [motion video URL] to [target image or video URL]. Keep the character on [position] and preserve [sound preference].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced character animation with spatial constraints

output_examples.input: Change a speaker's background to a neutral office and keep the original audio.
output: Selected Wan 2.7 Edit-Video for the background replacement.
Prioritized face, pose, lip movement, framing, and camera-motion preservation.

output_examples.input: Transfer a dance from a reference clip to a target character image.
output: Selected Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control for reference-based motion mapping.
Used image orientation and noted the ten-second output limit.
Included the requested character position and sound preference.

output_examples.input: Change the subject's outfit to business attire without changing the face.
output: Selected Lucy Edit Restyle for a localized outfit change.
Kept the instruction focused on outfit, face, and motion preservation.

best_practices: State preservation goals before describing the requested visual change.
Request one edit direction per call to reduce temporal drift.
Match source duration, format, resolution, and orientation to the selected route.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated outfit, background, lighting, and motion changes in one request.
Do not use Lucy Edit Restyle for complete character replacement.
Do not send sensitive media or long-lived signed URLs without reviewing RunComfy data handling.

faq.question: Which model is used by default?
faq.answer: Wan 2.7 Edit-Video is the default because it supports general edits and output up to 1080p.

faq.question: Can the skill transfer motion from another video?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes reference-based motion transfer to Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control.

faq.question: Can it preserve the original audio?
faq.answer: Yes. Wan and Kling expose options for retaining source sound when the selected route supports it.

faq.question: Does it support local video files?
faq.answer: The documented routes require accessible media URLs. The skill does not describe local file uploading.

faq.question: What output quality is available?
faq.answer: Wan supports up to 1080p. Lucy is limited to 720p, while route-specific Kling limits depend on orientation.

faq.question: Where is the RunComfy token stored?
faq.answer: RunComfy login stores it under the user's configuration directory with mode 0600. CI can use the RUNCOMFY_TOKEN environment variable.
